title: LDAP and 4D v12
author: Jesse Pina, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: PHP GET FULL RESPONSE for error handling

historical_commentary.text: This note leans on 4D v12's newly-introduced PHP Execute bridge to reach the PHP LDAP module, since 4D itself had no native LDAP or Active Directory commands at the time. That PHP-bridge approach is dated and clunky by modern standards, but LDAP/AD authentication remains a common integration need; today it would more likely be handled via a compiled plugin, a REST-based identity provider/SSO integration, or a scripted external process, rather than shelling out through 4D's PHP interpreter bridge.
related_updates: Later 4D Tech Note 'SSO with LDAP' (asset 77397) revisits LDAP/SSO integration with more current techniques
Modern deployments typically favor REST/OAuth-based SSO or dedicated LDAP plugins over the PHP Execute bridge
